newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's August industrial output fell sharply.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's August industrial output fell sharply.

text.p: Industrial production in Colombia, excluding coffee processing, fell 4.37 percent in August from the same month last year, the National Statistics Department (DANE) said.

It said the decline in industrial activity during the month, the last for which official figures are available, was the worst since 1990, when Colombia's economy was reeling from a wave of drug-related violence and political uncertainty.
DANE said industrial production including coffee processing fell 0.18 percent during the first eight months of 1996 compared to the same period in 1995.

High domestic interest rates, and the political crisis stemming from charges that President Ernesto Samper used drug money to finance his 1994 election campaign, have been cited as leading factors contributing to a sharp economic slowdown so far this year.

Underscoring the slowdown, a survey published in Sunday's editions of El Tiempo, Colombia's leading daily, showed that 63 percent of businessmen and industrialists had reported a drop in third quarter earnings compared with the same period last year.
A full 56 percent also reported a drop in sales.
The survey of 500 businessmen, conducted from Oct. 10-25 by the independent Yankelovich Acevedo y Asociados polling firm, has a margin for error of plus or minus 4.3 percentage points.

More than 40 percent of participants in the survey cited "uncertainty" as the leading problem dogging the Colombian economy and 56.5 percent said they expected the United States to impose economic sanctions against Colombia sometime in the near future.
U.S. officials led by Myles Frechette, the outspoken U.S. ambassador to Colombia, have hinted that sanctions could be applied in March.
